title: SoftBank Posts a $7B Loss as US Data Center Costs Swell, Alibaba Plans an IPO for Its T-Head Chip Unit, and Oura Acquires AI Care Startup Counsel Health for $625M
subhead: SoftBank Group logged a $7 billion loss driven by surging US AI data center construction expenses and tech equity swings; Alibaba disclosed confidential filings to spin off and list its T-Head semiconductor unit as a domestic rival to Nvidia; and smart-ring maker Oura agreed to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625 million while researchers found 35,000 exposed Grok Build apps leaking confidential SpaceX data.

sections.heading: SoftBank's $7B Loss, Alibaba's T-Head Chip IPO Plan, and US-China AI Risk Talks
sections.body:
SoftBank Group reported a $7 billion loss as ballooning capital expenditures on US artificial intelligence data centers and a pullback in high-multiple AI equities weighed heavily on its quarterly results (Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg). The strain on compute economics is also hitting model developers directly: Nvidia-backed AI startup Cohere is locked in an urgent struggle to secure sufficient AI computing capacity to train and deploy its enterprise models (Bloomberg). Meanwhile, Anthropic opened the Australian retail tranche of its planned blockbuster IPO on Wednesday, with regulatory filings showing that all seven Anthropic co-founders plan to cash out roughly $250 million each at the midpoint of the price range while retaining voting control of the company, even as startup PSI used an unreleased Anthropic model to solve a nearly two-decade-old quantum computing question and Anthropic rolled out Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data artifacts to challenge Microsoft Office (CNBC, TechCrunch, The Register).

In China's semiconductor sector, e-commerce and cloud giant Alibaba announced plans to spin off and publicly list its chip design subsidiary T-Head (PingTouGe)—revealing it had submitted a confidential listing filing in September—to scale domestic AI accelerators rivaling Nvidia (CNBC). On the diplomatic front, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated in New York that Washington and Beijing will cooperate on managing frontier AI risks and urged a strategy to 'de-risk, not decouple' while Chinese Ambassador Xie Feng emphasized mutual 'red lines' (Anadolu Agency, Reuters, Bloomberg, SCMP).
sections.whyItMatters: SoftBank's $7 billion loss alongside Cohere's compute crunch and Alibaba's T-Head chip IPO shows that the primary bottleneck in AI is shifting from software algorithms to data center capital and sovereign silicon supply.

sections.heading: Oura's $625M Counsel Health Acquisition, OpenAI's Odessia Deal, and New York's AI Safety Law
sections.body:
Weeks after indefinitely postponing its planned $2.2 billion public listing, smart-ring maker Oura agreed to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625 million, integrating automated clinical guidance directly into its wearable health platform (TechCrunch). In parallel, OpenAI acquired travel technology startup Odessia, founded by former Sonder chief executive Francis Davidson, and launched a beta 'Businesses' feature inside ChatGPT allowing enterprises to manage brand profiles, update product catalogs, and track user interaction analytics, while venture firm Proximal Ventures raised a $27.5 million debut fund for AI drug discovery (TechCrunch, Bloomberg HT).

Regulatory compliance requirements for frontier labs also tightened across the United States and Europe. New York State began enforcing its sweeping AI safety law—championed by Governor Kathy Hochul—which mandates that major developers including OpenAI and Anthropic register with state authorities, disclose safety protocols, and report critical incidents or face civil fines, while bipartisan lawmakers in Washington called for federal AI and quantum legislation in the next Congress (TechCrunch, Spectrum News, Nextgov/FCW). Internationally, the European Union announced rules requiring platforms to make addictive social media app features easier to switch off, Spain's government formally requested a national suspension of TikTok, and Brazil fined Meta $1.3 million for failing to comply with judicial orders amid President Lula's accusations of 'algorithmic manipulation' during October's elections (AFP, Habertürk, Le Monde).
sections.whyItMatters: New York's enforcement of mandatory AI safety registration and incident reporting creates a de facto national compliance standard for OpenAI and Anthropic ahead of federal congressional action.

sections.heading: 35,000 Grok Build Apps Leak SpaceX Data and Microsoft Patches Over 1,000 Bugs
sections.body:
A major AI coding security lapse surfaced after researchers discovered 35,000 web applications created with xAI's Grok Build coding agent left wide open on the public internet, leaking confidential credentials and internal files—including sensitive data belonging to SpaceX (Ars Technica). The exposure follows yesterday's disclosure of leaked `.claude` configuration files on GitHub and underscores growing enterprise risk from autonomous coding agents, prompting one security developer to release a defensive tool designed to 'blind' AI agents attempting automated reverse engineering, while a 14-year-old developer released an open-source multi-agent coordination tool called Autark (Ars Technica, The Register).

In enterprise infrastructure security, Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday bundle addressed more than 1,000 vulnerabilities across its software stack, including one actively exploited zero-day, while security teams warned that Barracuda Networks email security gateways are being targeted via critical root-privilege vulnerabilities (The Register). On the hardware and networking front, Amazon debuted mobile Ring Robotics security drones and indoor patrol robots slated for release in late 2026 and early 2027, Cisco pushed top-of-rack data center switching to 100G to handle dense multi-core server consolidation, VMware proposed a new CNCF standard for virtual machines in hybrid Kubernetes environments, and Seagate resurrected the SSD-HDD hybrid drive with its FireCuda Forge (Ars Technica, The Register).
sections.whyItMatters: Leaving 35,000 Grok Build applications publicly accessible—including internal SpaceX data—demonstrates that AI app-generation tools are deploying production code without basic authentication or secret-management guardrails.

sections.heading: Report Links Nvidia Spy Scandal to $7B in China Sales as Huang Apologizes to Staff
sections.body:
Fallout from the counterintelligence investigation into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang deepened after The Information reported that Huang's yearslong personal relationship with suspected Chinese intelligence operative Alice Huang enabled more than $7 billion in Nvidia AI chip sales to Chinese buyers, while the New York Times detailed how the suspected operative gained access to restricted Nvidia hardware (The Information, New York Times). According to the Wall Street Journal, Jensen Huang sent a company-wide letter on Sunday apologizing to Nvidia employees—including his own adult children on staff—for his infidelity, as Politico and the WSJ noted the scandal is testing investor confidence in the global AI boom and the South China Morning Post reported that Huang's attendance at next week's APEC summit in Shenzhen is now in doubt while Elon Musk is still expected to join President Trump (Wall Street Journal, Politico, CNA, Milliyet).

In consumer and legal tech news, Google rolled out its November Pixel Drop with Gemini-powered custom widgets and added an undisclosed second 5G carrier network to Google Fi, Apple introduced sign-language translation on Apple TV, Rockstar Games opened digital preloads for Grand Theft Auto VI nine days ahead of launch, and a San Francisco judge sentenced tech consultant Nima Momeni to 16 years to life in prison for the 2023 murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee (Ars Technica, Bloomberg HT, Anadolu Agency, The Guardian).
sections.whyItMatters: Investigative findings tying Jensen Huang's personal relationship directly to $7 billion in Chinese chip sales elevate the Nvidia affair from a corporate governance crisis into a major export-control and national security case.

bottomLine: Financial pressures, regulatory enforcement, and AI security breaches converged on Wednesday: SoftBank reported a $7 billion loss on rising US data center costs, Alibaba unveiled plans to list its T-Head semiconductor unit, and Anthropic opened its Australian retail IPO tranche with its seven co-founders set to cash out $250 million each. In digital health and consumer AI, Oura agreed to buy Counsel Health for $625 million, OpenAI acquired travel startup Odessia, and New York's AI safety law took effect. Meanwhile, researchers uncovered 35,000 exposed Grok Build apps leaking confidential SpaceX data, Microsoft patched over 1,000 bugs, and new reports linked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese operative to over $7 billion in China chip sales.
sources: Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, Reuters, CNBC, New York Times, The Information, Politico, TechCrunch, Ars Technica, The Register, The Guardian, Le Monde, AFP, CNA, SCMP, Anadolu Agency, Bloomberg HT, Habertürk, Milliyet
